task.title: Custom board names and color themes
task.description:
Every workbook board just says "Repository Workbench / Workbook board" in the header and the color scheme is the same.
This is inconvenient for anyone using Workbook for more than one project because you can't tell the webpages apart.

Now that we have custom project config, we want to add some properties to it to change these. The config should allow a custom project name, and two custom project colors: primary and text.

First, as a default, the "Repository Workbench" text should change to say "Repository: <repo name>" where `repo name` is derived from the directory of the user (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

When configured, the project name will display where the header currently says "Workbook board".

The Primary color replaces the current blue: rgb(36, 87, 214). The app should auto-generate complementary colors, for example the task header's rgb(213, 222, 234). The text color replaces the main rgb(23, 32, 51) for text.

Updating these values should be done under the `workbook config` command, with a web UI available on the current Statusus page, below the Status settings. The "Statuses" link should change to "Config".

## Shipped (2026-08-19, PRs #112 and #113)

Two PRs, each through a multi-round adversarial execution-verified review (records on the PRs).

PR #112 (core + ledger + CLI): display settings live in the config ledger as display.set/display.unset ops on a display section beside the vocabulary — nil-when-empty so every pre-existing checkpoint stays byte-identical (golden-pinned, proven both directions against a real v0.5.0-era binary). Writer-format generation bumped 1 -> 2: a v0.5.0 clone reads a display-configured project tolerantly and parks on write with exit 9 newer-writer, never corrupt-data. Concurrent edits to the same setting surface a display-setting conflict classified against the fork-point value (the review's second round found and killed both a silently-lost origin-side clear and spurious self-conflicts on multi-pack local chains). CLI: workbook config set/unset project-name|primary-color|text-color with exact inverses in results and status log, config show sources, colors canonicalized to lowercase #rrggbb. The review's biggest catch: a no-op unset originally authored a pack anyway, permanently parking v0.5.0 clones for a command that did nothing — no-ops now refuse with exit 5 and an unmoved ref.

PR #113 (web): eyebrow "Repository: <worktree dir>", configured name in the h1 and every tab title, /statuses renamed outright to /config (Dylan's call, no redirect), and the palette converted to --wb-* custom properties with the legacy literals as defaults — proven lossless three ways in real Chrome (computed styles, CSS substitution, pixel diff confined to the header). Custom accents derive the full family (hovers, focus rings, tints, hairlines, ink shadows) in Go via a chroma-based model: the review caught the HSL formula deriving a saturated yellow family from #fffffe while #ffffff derived greys; the fix carries channel-span chroma so one unit of color moves every token by at most 1, and the renderer was made total (malformed-hex-proof under a 400-case sweep). Board settings form on /config saves all three settings in one expectedHead-guarded pack, diffing canonicalized values so an idle Save writes nothing (the PR #112 lesson, verified against the actual git ref). Priority triad and danger/warning colors deliberately stay unthemed.

Residuals (accepted, recorded on the PRs): no contrast floor — a deliberately pale color renders a pale board, README says so and names config unset as the theme-independent recovery; a handful of defensive/cosmetic hunks untested, each exercised live in review.
